source_title: Championship roundup: Priske’s double gives Birmingham victory over Lincoln

Hammers fans angry after West Brom seal 3-1 victory
Hammers fans angry after West Brom seal 3-1 victory
Swansea win 4-0; Middlesbrough cruise against Charlton
Swansea win 4-0; Middlesbrough cruise against Charlton
Nuno Espirito Santo is facing mounting pressure after West Brom’s stylish 3-1 win at the London Stadium left West Ham , the Championship promotion favourites, six points off the pace in eighth place.
A second consecutive home defeat contained few saving graces for Nuno, who faced the wrath of fans on the final whistle. Albion, slick and measured, moved into the top four with their 3,000 travelling fans revelling in the discomfort of Nuno, once manager of arch-rivals Wolves.
After falling behind in nine of their previous 15 games, West Ham conceded first again on 20 minutes, with the unmarked midfielder Felix Horn Myhre firing home from point-blank range.
West Ham levelled when a Jarrod Bowen shot deflected in off Callum Styles, but within three minutes of the restart Albion were back in front. Jimmy-Jay Morgan1 struck his fourth goal of the season from the corner of the six-yard box.
Within two minutes of Walker-Peters limping off with a thigh injury, and with Nuno using up all his five substitutes, Price’s corner was only half-cleared to Styles and his fierce, deflected shot made it three.
Asked about visiting fans’ taunts that he would be “sacked in the morning”, Nuno said: “This is the reality: we can only change this if we win games. There is pressure every day. We have conceded six goals at home in two games and we have to fix it. The idea and the approach is to try and score first. That is the objective of any team and it’s our responsibility to change it.”
The in-form Will Lankshear scored twice as Middlesbrough maintained their position at the top with a comprehensive 3-0 victory over Charlton at the Riverside. Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Lankshear netted twice to take his tally to 15 in all competitions.
An overhead kick from Joe Low opened the scoring as League One leaders Huddersfield swept aside 10-man Bradford 3-0 in the West Yorkshire derby. Huddersfield went in front after four minutes and two goals in six minutes at the start of the second half from Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Joe Taylor killed off the contest at Valley Parade. The Bradford captain, Antoni Sarcevic, was sent off with a second yellow card in the 70th minute.
Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis ensured second-placed Stockport kept pace in a 2-1 comeback over AFC Wimbledon at Edgeley Park after Jayden Stockley broke the deadlock for the visitors in the 47th minute. Third-placed Oxford and Barnsley finished with 10 men in their 1-1 draw. Hosts Barnsley were left short-handed for the majority of the contest after Jack Shepherd was sent off in the ninth minute. Vimal Yoganathan’s 32nd-minute opener for Barnsley was cancelled out by Mark Harris on the hour, and the Us went down to 10 men after their goalkeeper, Jamie Cumming, was sent off with two minutes remaining in normal time.
Luton beat Peterborough 2-0, Plymouth played out a goalless draw with Reading , Leicester split the points in a 2-2 draw with Stevenage and Leyton Orient beat Cambridge 3-0. Notts County were 2-0 victors at Mansfield , MK Dons drubbed Doncaster 6-1, Wycombe won 2-0 against Burton and Wigan beat Bromley 3-2. Press Association
Swansea provided the perfect response to last Saturday’s hammering at QPR by beating Blackburn 4-0. The hosts were three goals to the good by half-time thanks to Stephen Eustáquio, Joseph Opoki and Filip Lissah, with the Scotland international striker Ross Stewart scoring his first goal for the Swans on the hour mark to complete the rout. Tony Mowbray’s Rovers had arrived in Wales having won four of their previous six games, including last week’s 2-0 home victory over Wrexham , but were blown away in the first half.
Headed goals from Fer Lopez, Adam Armstrong and Ladislav Krejci helped Wolves beat Cardiff 3-0 at Molineux. Wolves gave themselves the platform for victory by scoring twice in the first 15 minutes and made it four games unbeaten and back-to-back wins without conceding, ending Cardiff’s three-match unbeaten run.
Cameron Bragg scored his first Championship goal as Southampton made it 17 home league matches without losing with a 4-1 victory over QPR . Kuryu Matsuki, Keven Schlotterbeck and Welington also got on the scoresheet as Saints stayed fifth and kept pace with the leaders.
Two-goal August Priske was praised by his manager, Chris Davies, after the recalled Danish striker helped Birmingham beat Lincoln 3-1 at the ProAmpac Stadium. He scored either side of the break to take his season tally to seven, with Alex Cochrane securing the win after the Imps substitute Tom Bayliss had reduced the deficit.
“He gave us a real focal point, with his size and his strength,” said Davies. “He’s very mature for his age and he has all the tools, the temperament, the technical skills, the physicality and again he just needs to keep hungry, keep pushing.”
Mark Robins saluted his on-song Stoke side but admitted they could have been “more clinical” despite putting bottom side Preston to the sword with a comfortable 2-0 victory. Goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn did the damage as Stoke claimed a seventh victory in their past 10 league games.
Will Aimson scored a spectacular long-range goal as top-of-the-league Salford battled to a 2-1 win over in-form Exeter . The 32-year-old centre-back opened his Salford account in style two minutes from time after Luke Garbutt had cancelled out Sonny Cox’s first-half opener for the Grecians.
Barnet and Crewe drew 1-1, as did Accrington and Northampton , and Tranmere came from behind to secure their first home win since early September with an impressive 3-1 victory over Cheltenham at Prenton Park. A double from Dylan Jones and a stunning strike from Charlie Whitaker before the break overturned Charlie McCann’s early opener to give Rovers all three points.
Fleetwood followed their Carabao Cup win over Arsenal with a 3-1 victory over Bristol Rovers at Highbury. Matt Lawlor’s side picked up the three points thanks to goals from Aaron Loupalo-Bi, Rhys Bennett and Josh Roberston.
Colchester were dealt a 3-1 defeat by Walsall , Grimsby beat York 5-2, Swindon secured a 2-1 victory over Rotherham , Gillingham won 2-1 at Shrewsbury , Port Vale beat Rochdale 4-2, and Oldham fell 1-0 to Crawley . Press Association
Fabio Celestini’s tenure as Burnley head coach began with a 0-0 draw against Portsmouth at Turf Moor as the Clarets failed to capitalise on their first-half advantage. The Swiss manager, who celebrated his 51st birthday on Saturday, saw his side create a host of chances before the break, but a lack of clinical finishing ultimately cost them.
Kyrell Lisbie scored twice in the early stages as Millwall eased to a 4-1 victory against struggling Derby at The Den. The Lions scored three goals in the first 17 minutes to cruise to their second win in eight league games. It was another worrying afternoon for the Rams, though, who were never in the contest and remain second from bottom, four points from safety, and without a win in nine games.
Bristol City came from behind to stun Bolton 3-2 with an added-time Scott Twine winner. The visitors trailed 2-1 with six minutes of normal time remaining, but Sam Bell levelled before fellow substitute Twine ensured their manager, Michael Skubala, celebrated his 44th birthday with three points. City’s win was their first in five games while Bolton have now gone six weeks since their last success at home.
Alessio Dionisi hit out at his players after Watford surrendered a two-goal half-time lead to lose 3-2 at Norwich , increasing the pressure on his position. Watford looked well placed to take the points after Myron Boadu opened his account for the club with a well-taken double, but Norwich were a different side in the second half, and never looked back after Ben Chrisene had pulled one back in the 54th minute. Anthony Musaba raced through down the right to level the scores after 62 minutes and nine minutes later it was 3-2 as Paris Maghoma fired home.
“I am furious,” said Dionisi. “It is difficult to explain the difference between the first and second half. Football is crazy, I know that, but to lose a game like that – it’s impossible. There were nearly 1,300 Watford fans here today and I would like to be saying thank you for their support rather than saying sorry, again.”
On Friday, Ben Brereton Díaz’s first goal of the season sealed a deserved 1-0 win for Sheffield United against Wrexham at Bramall Lane. The Chile forward, in his third spell on loan with the Blades, struck the only goal in the first half.

## प्रमुख फुटबॉल मुकाबले और परिणाम
हाल ही में संपन्न हुए विभिन्न फुटबॉल मैचों में कई टीमों ने अपने प्रदर्शन से प्रभावित किया है। वेस्ट ब्रोम ने वेस्ट हैम के खिलाफ मुकाबले में 3-1 से जीत दर्ज की। इस हार के बाद वेस्ट हैम के प्रबंधक नूनो एस्पिरिटो सैंटो पर दबाव बढ़ने की खबरें सामने आई हैं, क्योंकि उनकी टीम अंक तालिका में आठवें स्थान पर खिसक गई है। मैच के दौरान वेस्ट ब्रोम के समर्थकों ने अपनी टीम की इस शानदार जीत का जश्न मनाया।

## अन्य महत्वपूर्ण मैच परिणाम
- **मिडल्सब्रॉ:** टीम ने चार्ल्टन के खिलाफ 3-0 से आसान जीत दर्ज की, जिसमें विल लैंकेशायर ने दो गोल दागे।
- **स्वान्सी:** स्वान्सी ने ब्लैकबर्न पर 4-0 से शानदार जीत हासिल करते हुए पिछले मैच की हार का करारा जवाब दिया।
- **वॉल्व्स:** वॉल्व्स ने कार्डिफ को 3-0 से हराकर अपने अजेय सिलसिले को जारी रखा।
- **बर्मिंघम:** ऑगस्ट प्रिस्क के दो गोल की बदौलत बर्मिंघम ने लिंकन को 3-1 से पराजित किया।

## प्रबंधकों की प्रतिक्रियाएं और स्थिति
मैच के बाद कई टीमों के प्रबंधकों ने अपनी प्रतिक्रिया दी। वेस्ट हैम के प्रबंधक नूनो ने स्वीकार किया कि टीम को घरेलू मैदान पर लगातार मिल रही हार से उबरने के लिए अपनी रणनीति में सुधार करना होगा और जीत की राह पर लौटना होगा। वहीं, बर्मिंघम के प्रबंधक क्रिस डेविस ने ऑगस्ट प्रिस्क के खेल की सराहना करते हुए उनकी शारीरिक क्षमता और परिपक्वता की तारीफ की।

## आगे की स्थिति और सत्यापन
इन मुकाबलों के विस्तृत आंकड़े और आधिकारिक घोषणाओं की पुष्टि के लिए संबंधित लीग की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट या खेल समाचार पोर्टलों की मदद ली जा सकती है।

## West Ham Fall to West Brom Amid Mounting Pressure

West Ham United manager Nuno Espirito Santo faced renewed pressure following a 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion at the London Stadium. The result leaves the pre-season promotion favourites six points off the pace in eighth place.

West Brom capitalized on defensive frailties after Felix Horn Myhre opened the scoring in the 20th minute. While Jarrod Bowen equalized via a deflection off Callum Styles, Albion regained control after the break through Jimmy-Jay Morgan and a second deflected effort from Styles.

* **Match outcome:** West Brom secured a 3-1 victory, moving into the top four.
* **Managerial pressure:** Nuno acknowledged the team's defensive struggles at home, noting they have conceded six goals across their last two fixtures at the London Stadium.

## Promotion Contenders Keep Pace Across the Divisions

At the summit of the Championship, Middlesbrough maintained their position with a 3-0 win against Charlton at the Riverside Stadium. Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring before Will Lankshear netted a brace, taking his tally to 15 goals across all competitions this season.

Elsewhere in the division:

* **Southampton** extended their unbeaten home run to 17 matches with a 4-1 victory over QPR.
* **Swansea City** rebounded from a heavy defeat the previous week to sweep aside Blackburn Rovers 4-0.
* **Wolves** secured a 3-0 win against Cardiff City at Molineux, courtesy of headed goals from Fer Lopez, Adam Armstrong, and Ladislav Krejci.
* **Millwall** cruised to a 4-1 win over struggling Derby County, thanks largely to two early goals from Kyrell Lisbie.

## League One and Lower Division Highlights

In League One, Huddersfield Town maintained their position at the top with a 3-0 victory in the West Yorkshire derby against 10-man Bradford City, featuring an opening overhead kick from Joe Low. Meanwhile, Salford City edged past Exeter City 2-1 thanks to a late long-range strike from Will Aimson.

*Note: Match outcomes and quotes are sourced from official matchday reports. Fans and observers can verify results and fixture schedules through official club channels and league governing bodies.*
